14. In April 1986, a disastrous nuclear accident happened at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Station. A large
quantity of various radioactive substances was released and spread to neighbouring countries. The
radiation levels recorded in these countries were much higher than the normal background count rate.

(a) State ONE source of background radiation. (1 mark)
(b) One of the radioactive isotopes released in the accident was caesium-137 (Cs-137). The
following equation shows how Cs-137 is produced :

2’Cs = 136.9071 u
2 Rb = 94.9399 u
pn == 1.0087 u
1 u is equivalent to 931 MeV

*@ii) The half-life of Cs-137 is 30 years. A soil sample contaminated by Cs-137 has an
